propositions.text: Seeks order staying her removal from Canada until judicial review is disposed of

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant seeks an order staying her removal from Canada until her judicial review is finally disposed of.

propositions.text: Underlying application relates to negative decision on Applicant's permanent residence request on H&C grounds
Application for Leave and Judicial Review filed Feb 8, 2021, perfected July 15, 2021
Applicant received Direction to Report for removal Oct 20, 2021; motion filed Oct 28, 2021

paragraphs.summary: The underlying application concerns a negative H&C decision; judicial review filed Feb 2021; removal scheduled; motion filed Oct 28, 2021.

propositions.text: Applicant is 44, Indian citizen, entered Canada as PR in Dec 2010 as spouse of skilled worker
Report under s 44 IRPA for serious criminality issued Aug 17, 2015; deportation order Sept 28, 2018; lost PR status
H&C application submitted June 5, 2019

paragraphs.summary: Applicant is a 44-year-old Indian citizen who lost PR status after serious criminality report and deportation order; H&C application filed June 2019.

propositions.text: Serious criminality was manslaughter conviction with 10-year sentence on July 31, 2015

paragraphs.summary: Applicant was convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to 10 years imprisonment in 2015.

propositions.text: Crime involved fatal brain injury to Applicant's 3-year-old child with multiple injuries
Child's condition on hospital arrival was horrific

paragraphs.summary: The crime involved fatal brain injury and multiple injuries to Applicant's 3-year-old child, with horrific condition on hospital arrival.

propositions.text: Applicant charged with second-degree murder but jury convicted manslaughter, implying killing was not intentional

paragraphs.summary: Applicant was charged with second-degree murder but convicted of manslaughter, indicating killing was not intentional.

propositions.text: Sentencing judge noted aggravating factors: victim vulnerability, repeated assaults, denial of responsibility, lack of remorse
No family spoke for child; court did so; no mitigating factors
Applicant may not have accepted responsibility; family claims she is blameless

paragraphs.summary: Sentencing judge noted aggravating factors and lack of mitigation; Applicant may not accept responsibility; family claims innocence.

propositions.text: Sentencing court considered immigration consequences modestly in sentencing
Deportation should not be additional punishment
Applicant benefitted somewhat from immigration consequences being considered in sentence length

paragraphs.summary: Sentencing court modestly considered immigration consequences; Applicant argues deportation is not punishment; she benefitted from this consideration.

propositions.text: Applicant had two other children removed at birth; they live with father and grandmother
Applicant released on parole with strict conditions including no contact with minors without supervision

paragraphs.summary: Applicant's other children were removed; she is on parole with strict no-contact conditions with minors.

propositions.text: Applicant filed extensive updated submissions for H&C between June 2019 and Sept 2020
Applicant's affidavit diminishes responsibility despite jury verdict and trial findings

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submitted extensive updated H&C materials but continues to diminish responsibility for crime in affidavit.

propositions.text: Submissions included letters of support and rehabilitation reports
Grounds include establishment, family ties, best interests of surviving children, hardship in India
Applicant is Brahmin but claims not accepted by husband's family due to cultural norms

paragraphs.summary: Applicant's submissions include support letters and rehabilitation; claims hardship and family rejection in India despite Brahmin status.

propositions.text: Senior Immigration Officer reviewed background, offence nature, and Applicant's materials
Officer addressed each ground raised by Applicant

paragraphs.summary: Senior Immigration Officer reviewed all materials and addressed each ground raised by Applicant.

propositions.text: Officer erred by applying incorrect test on circumstances, establishment, children's best interests, and hardship evidence

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Officer erred in applying incorrect test on circumstances, establishment, children's best interests, and hardship evidence.

propositions.text: Whether Court should make Anonymization Order
Whether Applicant satisfied test for interlocutory injunction

paragraphs.summary: Issues: whether to make Anonymization Order and whether Applicant satisfied interlocutory injunction test.

propositions.text: Requested anonymization order for Applicant, husband, and children in public documents

paragraphs.summary: Applicant requests anonymization order for herself, husband, and children in public documents.

propositions.text: Criminal trial had substantial media attention; publication may harm children's health
Trial judge banned publication of surviving children's names

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submits media attention and publication may harm children; trial judge banned publication of children's names.

propositions.text: Strong presumption of open courts; high bar for anonymization or redactions
Open court principle from Sherman Estate v Donovan, 2021 SCC 25 paras 2-3

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues strong open court presumption and high bar for anonymization, citing Sherman Estate v Donovan.

propositions.text: Applicant's request is overly broad as crime facts are public
If only Applicant concerned, request would be refused
Request concerns children; evidence shows oldest child suffered from publicity

paragraphs.summary: Court finds request overly broad but accepts concern for children, especially oldest child suffering from publicity.

propositions.text: Orders anonymization of Applicant's name by initials in style of cause and subsequent proceedings
No order for redaction of identities of Applicant and family members now; may revisit if judicial review proceeds

paragraphs.summary: Court orders anonymization of Applicant's name by initials; no redaction of family identities now but may revisit later.

propositions.text: Stay motion requires conjunctive tripartite test from Manitoba v Metropolitan Stores and Toth
Test: serious issue to be tried, irreparable harm, balance of convenience
Principles confirmed by Supreme Court in RJR MacDonald and R v Canadian Broadcasting Corp

paragraphs.summary: Court states stay motion requires tripartite test: serious issue, irreparable harm, balance of convenience, confirmed by Supreme Court.

propositions.text: The threshold for a serious issue to be tried is low; case must not be frivolous or vexatious; minimal inquiry required

paragraphs.summary: The court states the low threshold for a serious issue to be tried requires minimal inquiry and the case must not be frivolous or vexatious.

propositions.text: Officer erred by assessing circumstances only through hardship and importing exceptionality into relief test
Officer erred by applying hardship as test for best interests of surviving children, not being sensitive as required by Kanthasamy

paragraphs.summary: The applicant argues the officer erred by focusing only on hardship and misapplying the best interests test for children per Kanthasamy.

propositions.text: H&C decision is reasonable; officer considered all factors and gave reasons for refusal
Respondent addresses each of applicant's alleged errors in turn

paragraphs.summary: The respondent contends the H&C decision was reasonable and addresses each of the applicant's alleged errors.

propositions.text: Officer's reasons are thorough; court's role is minimal inquiry, not merits assessment
Applicant's arguments are not frivolous or vexatious and constitute serious issues to be tried

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the officer's reasons thorough and concludes the applicant's arguments raise serious issues to be tried.

propositions.text: Applicant will face irreparable harm if removed before judicial review; cites Toth decision on irreparable harm

paragraphs.summary: The applicant submits she will face irreparable harm if removed before judicial review, citing Toth decision.

propositions.text: More than reasonable likelihood of harm required; irreparable harm must be shown with convincing evidence
Glooscap Heritage Society requires real probability of unavoidable irreparable harm, not speculation

paragraphs.summary: The respondent argues irreparable harm requires convincing evidence of real probability, citing Glooscap Heritage Society.

propositions.text: Justice Norris in Kambasaya explains irreparable harm means harm not remediable if stay refused
Irreparable harm concerns nature, not magnitude; must be real, definite, unavoidable, not speculative
Applicant must provide clear, non-speculative evidence of irreparable harm; unsubstantiated assertions insufficient

paragraphs.summary: Justice Norris in Kambasaya clarifies irreparable harm requires real, unavoidable harm with clear evidence, not speculation.

propositions.text: Applicant and children face irreparable harm from removal; family would not follow to India
Children deprived of daily contact due to time differences and communication difficulties with rural India

paragraphs.summary: The applicant argues removal causes irreparable harm as family won't follow and children lose daily contact due to distance.

propositions.text: Oldest child has disorders from traumatic events; health would deteriorate if mother removed
Applicant suffers mental disorders treated in custody; inadequate treatment expected in India
Removal causes extended family separation; return to Canada requires pardon and approvals, unavailable for 10 years

paragraphs.summary: Applicant claims oldest child's health and her own mental health would worsen if removed; separation would be prolonged due to return barriers.

propositions.text: Removal would render judicial review proceedings illusory and reduce chances of success on redetermination
Even if readmitted later, harm from family separation would have occurred

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues removal would make judicial review ineffective and cause irreversible family separation harm.

propositions.text: Applicant could rely on extended family in India and maintain ties via technology
Potential mootness of litigation does not alone establish irreparable harm warranting stay
Cites El Ouardi, Palka, Shpati cases supporting respondent's position

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues applicant can rely on family and technology; mootness alone insufficient for irreparable harm, citing cases.

propositions.text: Kambasaya notes jurisprudence on removal during pending H&C does not address removal after refusal during judicial review

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Kambasaya distinguishes removal during pending H&C from removal after refusal during judicial review.

propositions.text: Normal consequences of deportation like family separation and cultural readjustment do not constitute irreparable harm
Outstanding H&C application alone insufficient to establish irreparable harm

paragraphs.summary: The court finds normal deportation consequences and pending H&C application do not amount to irreparable harm.

propositions.text: Removal before decision on leave and judicial review would cause irreparable harm to applicant in these circumstances

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes removal before judicial decisions would cause irreparable harm to the applicant here.

propositions.text: Public interest favors prompt execution of removal orders, especially for serious criminality
Public interest must be considered in stay of removal decisions

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues public interest favors prompt removal; court agrees public interest must be considered.

propositions.text: Underlying crime is shocking and troubling
Public interest also requires remedies to be meaningful and effective
Applicant raised non-frivolous issues and would suffer irreparable harm if removed before court consideration
Application perfected and decision on leave imminent are relevant factors

paragraphs.summary: Court finds crime shocking but public interest requires effective remedies; applicant's serious issues and irreparable harm support stay.

propositions.text: Applicant has no prior criminal history and is not a risk to reoffend
Applicant remains on parole and strict supervision pending judicial review outcome
Balance of convenience favors applicant; stay of removal should be granted

paragraphs.summary: Court finds applicant low risk, under supervision, and balance of convenience favors granting stay of removal.
